title: Unified Memory Protection with Multi-granular MAC and Integrity Tree for Heterogeneous Processors
problem: Hardware memory protection in heterogeneous SoCs (CPU + GPU + NPU) causes significant performance degradation because conventional fixed-granularity MACs and integrity trees are optimized for CPU access patterns but perform poorly under the diverse, irregular memory access patterns of GPUs and NPUs.
motivation: Edge SoCs increasingly integrate heterogeneous processing units with strict security requirements, but existing domain-specific memory protection techniques that customize granularity for either counters or MACs—but not both—cannot efficiently handle all processing unit access patterns simultaneously.
method: The system protects memory by storing authentication codes (small checksums that verify data hasn't been corrupted) organized in a tree. Rather than protecting all memory in fixed-size chunks, it dynamically chooses from four different chunk sizes based on how each processor actually accesses memory—CPUs prefer large chunks while GPUs work better with smaller ones. A detection mechanism watches each processing unit's access patterns and selects the best chunk size per memory region. It also incorporates existing tree optimizations to reduce the cost of checking these authentication codes.
key_novelty: Instead of using fixed chunk sizes for memory protection, this approach dynamically adjusts both the authentication code and counter chunk sizes at the same time based on each processor's access patterns, making it efficient across CPU, GPU, and NPU workloads.
contributions: Unified multi-granular MAC and integrity tree mechanism supporting four granularity levels
Dynamic detection mechanism selecting optimal granularity per memory region and processing unit type
14.2% execution time reduction over conventional fixed-granular MAC and tree
21.1% execution time reduction when combined with prior sub-tree techniques

metrics.speedup: 14.2% execution time reduction over fixed-granular MAC and tree; 21.1% with sub-tree techniques

baselines: Conventional fixed-granular MAC and integrity tree
limitations: Simulation-based evaluation; physical implementation overhead of dynamic granularity detection logic is not discussed.
primary_theme: Adaptive multi-granular memory integrity protection for heterogeneous SoC processors
